questions.question: The number of valence electrons of P and Si are ______ respectively.
questions.explanation:
Phosphorus has five valence electrons.
Silicon has four valence electrons.
questions.subject: basic-electronics

questions.question: Semiconductors have ______ conduction band and ______ valence band.
options: A lightly filled, a moderately filled
An almost filled, a moderately filled
An almost empty, an almost filled
An almost filled, an almost empty
questions.answer: An almost empty, an almost filled
questions.correctAnswer: An almost empty, an almost filled
questions.explanation:
A semiconductor has an almost empty conduction band.
Its valence band is almost filled.
questions.subject: basic-electronics

questions.question: The temperature coefficient of resistance in a pure semiconductor is ______.
questions.explanation:
Pure semiconductors have negative temperature coefficient.
Their resistance decreases when temperature increases.
questions.subject: basic-electronics

questions.question: Valence electrons are the ______.
options: Electrons present in the outermost orbit
Electrons that do not carry any charge
questions.answer: Electrons present in the outermost orbit

questions.explanation:
Valence electrons are in the outermost orbit.
They take part in bonding and conduction.

questions.question: At room temperature intrinsic carrier concentration is higher in germanium than silicon because ______.
options: Carrier mobilities are higher in Ge than Si
Energy gap in Ge is smaller than that in Si
Atomic number of Ge is larger than Si
Atomic weight of Ge is larger than Si
questions.answer: Energy gap in Ge is smaller than that in Si

questions.explanation:
Germanium has smaller energy gap than silicon.
Smaller energy gap gives more carriers at room temperature.

questions.question: What will be the resistance of a semiconductor at a low temperature?
questions.explanation:
At low temperature, few charge carriers are available.
So semiconductor resistance becomes high.

Extrinsic semiconductor is made by doping.

Doping means adding impurity.

P-type semiconductor has more holes.

questions.question: In n-type semiconductor, which carriers are minority carriers?
questions.explanation:
Electrons are majority carriers in n-type.

questions.question: In p-type semiconductor, which carriers are minority carriers?
questions.explanation:
Holes are majority carriers in p-type.
So electrons are minority carriers.
